1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons __based on a predetermined safety protocol that evaluates multiple system states before enabling weapon release__.

2. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons interface includes a first weapons interface to a first weapon and a second weapons interface to a second weapon, the first weapon and the second weapon being of different types.

3. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 2 wherein: the weapons interface includes a third weapons interface to a third weapon and a fourth weapons interface to a fourth weapon, the third weapon and the fourth weapon being of different types.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard __and implements interlock logic that prevents fire signal transmission until all safety conditions are satisfied__.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel __and controlled through a dedicated laser arm switch on a control panel of the weapons stores processor panel__.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display __and provides real-time weapons status information to the display__.

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position __wherein the master arm switch position directly controls power distribution to the weapons interface controller and enables or disables fire signal generation__.

8. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

9. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

10. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

11. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __and the laser arm switch operates independently from the master arm switch__.

12. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position.

13. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 12 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system __and implements a separate safety interlock specific to manual override mode__.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display __and the display information includes real-time safety interlock status__.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons __and the weapons stores processor panel validates all safety interlock conditions before authorizing the weapons bus controller to execute firing commands__.

17. (Currently amended) A vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) rotary-wing aircraft comprising: an aircraft mounted weapon; and an aircraft weapons control system, the aircraft weapons control system including: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of the aircraft weapon; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapon __based on a predetermined safety protocol that evaluates multiple system states before enabling weapon release__.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel __and controlled through a dedicated laser arm switch on a control panel of the weapons stores processor panel__.

19. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position __wherein the master arm switch position directly controls power distribution to the weapons interface controller and enables or disables fire signal generation__.

20. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

21. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

22. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

23. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim of claim 19 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __and the laser arm switch operates independently from the master arm switch__.

24. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position.

25. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 24 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system __and implements a separate safety interlock specific to manual override mode__.

26. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire in a manual over-ride mode, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.
